- **Claim c1**: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, leading to an increase in cases where 5G was installed, is a conspiracy theory that has been widely debunked by scientific experts and international organizations. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]
- The International Telecommunications Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed in April 2020 that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling the theory "a hoax that has no technical basis." [2]
- Viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks, and COVID-19 has spread in many countries that do not have 5G networks. [3] [6] [7] [8]
- Experts, including the vice chairman of the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection, have stated that it is physically impossible for electromagnetic fields to transfer particles like viruses. [3]
- There is no scientific evidence to suggest that 5G compromises the immune system or enables people to get sick from COVID-19. [3] [5] [9]
- Despite the lack of evidence, this conspiracy theory led to dozens of arson attacks on 5G towers and harassment of mobile phone engineers in several European countries in 2020. [2] [3] [4] [5]
- Organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO), the US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and the UK government have all actively dispelled the myth, stating there is no link between 5G and coronavirus. [3] [6] [7]
